info.name: Heirloom App Backend
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Heirloom App backend (Express + TypeScript + MongoDB).

## Getting started
1. Import the companion environment files (`Heirloom - Local`, `Heirloom - Production`) or just edit the collection variables.
2. Run **Auth > Login** (or **Auth > Admin Login**) — the JWT is captured automatically into `{{token}}` / `{{adminToken}}` by the request test script.
3. Every other request inherits Bearer auth from the collection, so it just works.

## Auth model
- All protected routes read `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`.
- `guardRole(...)` restricts by the `role` claim in the JWT (`admin` | `manager` | `user`). Admin-only requests in this collection use `{{adminToken}}`.
- Token lifetime is 7 days. Expired/invalid tokens return **498 Session Expired**.

## OTP flows
- `register` and `forget-password` return a short-lived (1h) token in `data.token` → captured as `{{otpToken}}`.
- `verify-otp` must be sent with `Authorization: Bearer {{otpToken}}` and returns a full user token → captured as `{{token}}`.
- `reset-password` must be sent with the token returned by `verify-otp`.

## Base path
All API routes are mounted under `/api/v1`. Uploaded files are served statically from `/images/...`.

request.description: Note: this is declared as a **GET** route in `BookMark.route.ts` even though it creates a record.

item.name: Journals
item.description:
Mounted at `/api/v1/journals`. All routes require `role === "user"`.

Journal content is chunked and embedded into Pinecone on create — this is what gives the AI assistant its memory of the user.

request.description:
All three fields are required by the schema.

`title` has a **unique** index across the whole collection, so a duplicate title fails with a Mongo duplicate-key error. `customDate` is parsed with `new Date(...)`, so any ISO-8601 string works.

query.description: Optional. Case-insensitive regex match on title and content.

item.name: Legacy
item.description:
Mounted at `/api/v1/legacy`. All routes require `role === "user"`.

A legacy message is queued in Bull and delivered to its recipients at `triggerDate`.

request.description:
Controller validation:
- `recipients` — array of user ids, must not be empty
- `messages` — required, non-blank
- `type` — required, `onetime` | `loop`
- `triggerDate` — required and **must be in the future**, otherwise **400 "Time must be in the future"**
Legacies created by the authenticated user that have not fired yet.
Legacies that have already been delivered.
Re-schedules the queued Bull job when `triggerDate` changes. `type` is not editable through this endpoint.

item.name: Friends
item.description:
Mounted at `/api/v1/friend`. All routes require `role === "user"`.

**Relation values:** friend, mother, father, sister, brother, son, daughter, grandmother, grandfather, grandson, granddaughter, aunt, uncle, cousin, nephew, niece, mother-in-law, father-in-law, brother-in-law, sister-in-law, stepmother, stepfather, stepbrother, stepsister.

**Status values:** unfriended, requested, accepted, rejected.

request.description:
- `reciveBy` — id of the user receiving the request (note the spelling used by the API)
- `relation` — one of the relation enum values listed on this folder
Accepted connections for the authenticated user.
The decision is passed as the `status` **query param**; the friend-request document id is the path param.
Changes the relationship label on an existing connection.
Role: `user`. Directory search for people to connect with. The path is spelled `pepole` in the route definition.

item.name: Messages
item.description:
Mounted at `/api/v1/message`. All routes require `role === "user"`.

Real-time delivery happens over Socket.IO; these REST endpoints persist and fetch history. When the receiver has AI mode on, the backend generates and emits an AI reply in the background.

formdata.description: Receiver user id (schema field is spelled `reciver`).
Message text. Required unless an image is attached.

request.description:
Errors:
- **400 Missing conversation** — `conversation` not supplied
- **400 Missing message content** — neither `messages` nor a file
- **400 AI mode is active** — the sender has AI mode enabled on this conversation
Turns the AI stand-in on/off for the caller within a conversation. `conversationId` is required (**400** otherwise); `status` is a boolean.
Paginated message history, newest first.
Images shared inside the conversation.
Grouped inbox view for the authenticated user.
Standalone upload helper. Returns **404** when no file is attached. The returned `publicFileURL` is servable from `{{baseUrl}}` (static `public/` folder).

item.name: Assistant
item.description:
Mounted at `/api/v1/assistant`. Requires `role === "user"`.

The assistant answers using the user's journal entries retrieved from Pinecone.

request.description:
The user's prompt goes in the **`me`** field (required, **400** otherwise).

The reply is generated asynchronously — the HTTP response only echoes your message. Poll **My Conversations** or listen on the socket for the assistant's answer.
Roles: `admin`, `user`. Rewrites and polishes the supplied `content` with OpenAI and returns the enhanced text.

item.name: Notifications
item.description:
Mounted at `/api/v1/notification`.

`GET /` and `GET /badge-count` carry no route-level guard, but their controllers verify the bearer token themselves — a valid token is still required.

request.description: Admins receive the admin notification stream (`adminMsg`); everyone else receives the user stream (`userMsg`).
Admin only. Broadcasts an FCM push to the supplied device tokens via firebase-admin.

item.name: Report
item.description: Mounted at `/api/v1/report`. Users report other users; admins read and reply.

request.description:
No route-level role guard, but the controller requires a valid bearer token.

- `:suspectId` — the reported user's id
- `msgTitle` — required (**400 "What kind of report ?"**)
- `reportMsg` — required (**400 "Describe your issue!"**)
